chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Qurashi al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Harun ibn Kharijah, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him say: While al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) was with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to him and said, 'O Muhammad! Do you love him?' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Verily, your nation will kill him.' So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was extremely grieved. Jabra'il said to him, 'O Messenger of Allah! Do you wish [that it pleases you] for me to show you the land on which he will be killed?' He said, 'Yes.' Then the land between the place where the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was sitting and Karbala sank into the ground until the two pieces met like this. Then he brought his two index fingers together. Then Jabra'il picked up some of the dust with his wing and handed it to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). Then it returned faster than a blink of an eye. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to it, 'Blissful is you, O dust, and blissful is he who will be killed on you!'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad see when Jabra'il showed him the land of Karbala?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, the Angel Jibra'il reveals the specific geography of Karbala to the Prophet Muhammad, physically connecting his seat to the future battlefield to emphasize the divine predestination of Imam al-Husayn's martyrdom. The Prophet's profound grief is immediately followed by the gift of the earth, which serves as a tangible symbol of sanctity and a focal point for devotional visitation (ziyarat) in Shia tradition. This event underscores the spiritual significance of Karbala not merely as a historical site, but as a sacred locus where divine promise and human sacrifice intersect.
